title: Fix your hook in 4 videos
intro: A hook often comes from a very strong grip or a clubface that closes too fast relative to the path. This short path begins with the driver basics, then fixes the grip and works on path with two drills.

items.note: A pre-swing routine that golfers say sorted both slice and hook driver misses.

A trail arm drill to deal with the inside takeaway that can feed a hook.

title: Stop the shanks in 5 videos
intro: Shanks come from the ball hitting the hosel, usually because the hands or body move toward the ball through impact. This path explains what is happening, gives quick fixes, then drills and a rotation fix for the cause.

items.note: Butch Harmon explains hosel hits versus open-toe shots, so you know what you are fixing.
Stand taller, weight off your toes. Golfers say that was it.
More drills in the same spirit, praised as a best shank video.
The two ball drill trains the hand path so the shank stops showing up.
If you shank from sliding forward, this rotation drill addresses the weight shift behind it.

title: Strike your irons cleanly in 6 videos
intro: Thin, fat and weak iron contact often come from scooping, a poorly placed low point, or misunderstanding shaft lean. This path starts with the big ideas, then covers impact position, then drills to feel compression.

items.note: A myth-busting look at impact angles that golfers say helped most with tops and compression.

title: Fix early extension in 6 videos
intro: Early extension is when the hips thrust toward the ball in the downswing, which crowds your arms. This path shows what it looks like, how setup and hip depth cause it, then drills to keep your space.

items.note: The most recommended illustration of pros versus amateurs and how the hips should move.

title: Fix your over-the-top swing in 6 videos
intro: Over the top means the club moves out and across on the way down, usually because the arms and shoulders start the downswing. This path explains the move, shows how to shallow the club, then gives drills.

items.note: A starting point that explains the out-to-in loop and why exaggerating helps.

The two stick drill to groove a shallower delivery.

title: Stop casting the club in 5 videos
intro: Casting means releasing the wrist angle too early, which loses speed and strike quality. This path explains what is going on, then moves through drills for keeping the angle and releasing at the right time.

items.note: Why you cast the club, and how holding the hinge helps.

intro: Swaying means sliding sideways in the backswing instead of loading into your trail side. This path teaches how pressure moves, how to recenter, and then drills to stop the reverse pivot.

intro: A good takeaway sets up the rest of the swing, and common faults are outside paths, early wrist hinge and arms lifting. This path starts with how the arms and body move together, then moves to drills for the takeaway.

intro: The transition is the move from backswing to downswing, and common mistakes are starting with the arms instead of the lower body. This path explains sequencing, then shows how to drop the arms into the slot.

items.note: The most recommended video, explaining sequencing with Justin Rose's drill.
